title: A Generalized Unit Hydrograph Theory for Dynamic River Networks
content:
Abstract

The instantaneous unit hydrograph (IUH) synthetically describes how effective rainfall is transformed into discharge at the catchment outlet. According to classical geomorphological theories, the IUH is regarded as a time-invariant probability density function of watershed response times, an interpretation that implicitly postulates a fixed configuration of the channel network. However, river networks dynamically expand and contract, leading to systematic temporal variations in response times that challenge the foundations of standard IUH approaches. Here, we develop a generalized unit hydrograph theory that explicitly accounts for time-varying river networks. The proposed framework introduces a dynamic formulation of the convolution relationship linking effective rainfall and streamflow, applicable when active network length varies during and across events. In this case, the rainfall–runoff kernel can be decomposed into two components: the classical IUH contribution evaluated on the instantaneous network configuration and an additional dynamic term capturing the effects of temporal changes in flowing stream length. Numerical applications show that, across the explored configurations, network dynamics reshape the hydrological response of catchments and the associated flow-duration curves, in particular by increasing flood peaks and slowing down recessions. This pattern is confirmed by a proof-of-concept application to a monitored rainfall–runoff event in the Valfredda catchment (northeastern Italy), which achieved reasonably good performance and illustrates the potential of the proposed framework in real-world settings. The proposed framework bridges classical unit hydrograph theory and empirical evidence on channel network dynamics, providing a new pathway for representing catchment functioning in hydrological models.
